rows.grounds: object of punishment; past participle used substantively
instrumental indicating means of punishment; compound dhana-ādāna

items.question: What penalty should a king who pleases his subjects impose on an intoxicated offender?
premises: An intoxicated person is liable to punishment.
The king is characterized as one who causes delight to subjects.
Confiscation of wealth is specified as the means of punishment.
items.inference: A king who pleases his subjects should punish an intoxicated offender by confiscating wealth.
uncertainties: Whether mattaṃ refers specifically to drunkenness or intoxication in a broader sense is not explicit.
items.plain_english: A king who brings joy to his subjects should punish an intoxicated person by confiscating his wealth.
